p2.text: Part 2 — New design: read-only Files, beside Changes

p2note.text:
Part 2: decisions
• Changes and Diff match what shipped (⋯ ▸ Changes). New: the Files | Changes switch and the viewers. The file bar under a diff and Go to file are Proposed and optional (the Diff board has a switch).
• One read-only sheet. Done closes it; the voice carries on.
• Changes means this folder's uncommitted changes, by any agent. git can't tell who wrote what, so the copy says so, and agents sharing shop see one list.
• Search is file names only. Recently changed uses file times.
• This computer only, like the window button.
• Code and diff text stop at 28 pt at the largest size; Markdown grows in full.
• iPad: full screen, list beside viewer, in place of the sidebar.

Open questions
1. Files needs new read-only daemon routes, limited to the space's folder. Hidden for safety is drawn in Files, but changes.go has no such filter today, so a tracked .env can still show in Changes. Filter it there too?
2. Changes is per agent today. A space with no agents needs its own route.
3. Is 2 MB the right limit for the phone?
4. May text or images be shared out of the app? This draft stores nothing on the phone.
5. Should Changes mark the files an agent's journal lists?
6. Files for agents on another computer?

p3b.text: Factory — every state, dark and largest text

p3note.text:
Part 3: decisions
Each line says what a board reuses and what is new. New means proposed, not built.

Agents list
• Reuses: the Needs you / Working / Done sections and their one sort, the agent card, the crossed bell, the dock. New: role, task id and model on a factory row (the app must first read labels); the words Factory, not announced where VoiceOver now says Muted space; A worker stuck at a prompt is restarted by the engine; there is no card for it. No Factory group.
• The coordinator is silent, like the workers. If it is stuck twice in a row you are told once.

Window
• Reuses the whole Agent window. New: one line with the model.

Ask
• Reuses the approval card as it is: every option outlined, a Recommended tag, never a fill. New: the card also shows under Needs you on Agents, with the badge, and at the top of the factory section. One card, drawn once. An override is the same card with its own kind; only you can answer it.

Conversation
• Reuses ChatRow kinds only. A digest is the voice bubble with Details; an alert is an agent-update row.

Space page
• Reuses the Spaces sheet and its space page on phone and iPad. On iPad it stays the form sheet; no new detail screen.
• Two states. No factory: today's page plus one row, Start a factory here. With a factory: a Factory section at the top with the ask, the milestone, and tasks in dependency layers with the critical path in ink and the model on each row. A row with a live terminal opens its window; one without does nothing.
• The engine keeps one record per project; a space has a factory when its folder has one. The section survives the start shell closing.
• Close space is refused while the project's coordinator is alive. Stop the factory first: one new action, by voice or sheepdog factory stop. A factory you stopped stays stopped, with no alert, until you start it again from the same row.
• Debug is not on the page yet. It is drawn once, expanded, for the later task.

Starting
• Reuses Run a command: the row runs sheepdog factory start in a new tab of the space and opens its window. No new screen.
• In that terminal: doctor's lines at phone width with a fix under each failing one, the notice, then at most five prompts. Return accepts the recommended answer. An answer that would delegate a gate or a release only proposes it; it takes effect after one ask card answered by tap, by voice, or on the factory page.
• Stops the start: no signed-in CLI, not a git repository, gh not signed in, no pull-request workflow in the repo, a required approving review on the base, a factory already running there.
• By voice: Sheepdog reads back the project and the goal, and on a yes runs one fixed command with the recommended answers. It speaks one line if the check fails. Prompts in the terminal are typed, not spoken.
• The row is greyed, with the reason, when the phone shell is off or the folder is outside your project folders.

States
• Every state is the real section: no ask, planning, finished, stopped, stopped by you, could not load, the end of the page, and Debug open. Light and dark, plus one board at the largest text size.

Terminal and diagrams
• factory log (new) and factory doctor (exists; gains a Running now part), at phone width.
• Architecture, one task's lifecycle, the design loop.

Not drawn, on purpose: a task board, a chat with workers, per-worker narration, a factory group in the Agents list, a new iPad detail screen. The factory page on the web is Part 4; it is built before the phone.

p4bnote.text:
Part 4b: decisions (slice 14, PR 14.0, round 2)
Drawn from the page as built (web/factory), not from the older home board: no send box, no usage pools. New means proposed, not built.

• Where things live. Main column: tasks with the list / graph switch, the goal, the project bar (state word, one sentence, only that state's actions), the task groups, log, settings. Under 760 px the order is: tasks and project bar, asks for you, the task groups, log, projects, settings, agents. Aside: projects (state word on each line, New project under the list), asks for you, agents.
• New project opens a form in the main column, like the task view. Its models and max running rows are the settings rows with the defaults; nothing is stored before the start, so no Change and no read-back there.
• Start checks show the check's own name, detail and fix. A fix that starts "run:" is a block with Copy, marked "in a terminal"; the block holds the command only, up to the first " (" or ", then ", and the rest is text under it.
• Pairing: one box, opened beside the control that needed it. What was asked for is kept and sent after Pair. The missing-app help is a fold that is always there, because the page cannot see the menu bar.
• Stop always asks first, in place. Focus lands on Keep it running. The page gives no count and no roles of running agents.
• Settings: a row gets its Change button only while its field differs from the stored value; the read-back takes the row's place until answered. Save is recommended: bold outline and the word, never a fill (one orange button per screen: Start, or New project on the empty page).
• Steps: words and icons, never colour alone. A fifth state, ended, for the last step of a dropped or closed task; parked is the now step with its text. The compact bar always has the current step written beside it.
• Log marks: merged, held up, asked you, you. The toggle is "show routine checks".
• Graph view takes the full width; the aside cards move under it. Nodes keep one size, so a wide layer scrolls inside the graph's own box. Focus or hover draws a node's own edges and neighbours strong and dims the rest.
• Each light board has a dark copy and a 360 px copy below it.

Open questions are in docs/dev/design/canvas/slice14-wording.md and the design report.
